stem: Your development team has created a mobile game app. You want to test the new mobile app on Android and iOS devices with a variety of configurations. You need to ensure that testing is efficient and cost-effective. What should you do?
options: Upload your mobile app to the Firebase Test Lab, and test the mobile app on Android and iOS devices.
Create Android and iOS VMs on Google Cloud, install the mobile app on the VMs, and test the mobile app.
Create Android and iOS containers on Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE), install the mobile app on thecontainers, and test the mobile app.
Upload your mobile app with different configurations to Firebase Hosting and test each configuration.
explain: Firebase Test Lab exercises supported Android and iOS device configurations. Hosting files or creating generic Linux VMs does not provide the same mobile device test matrix.

stem: A new game running on Google Cloud must read selected data from a legacy game's Firestore database in another project. What should the team do to minimize privileges?
options: Grant its workload identity the required database-read permissions on the legacy project at the supported narrow scope.
Grant Organization Administrator and Firebase Administrator across both projects.
Move all games into one project so IAM is unnecessary.
Embed one downloadable service account private key in every client installation.
explain: Grant the new game's workload identity only the required Firestore permissions on the legacy project's database. There is no need to move projects or grant organization-wide or broad Firebase administrator access.

stem: A security team must run an authorized automated penetration test immediately after each successful application deployment. What trigger best follows the actual release event?
options: Publish a deployment-completion event to Pub/Sub and trigger the authenticated test function.
Run an unrelated weekly cron even if deployment has failed.
Run the test whenever a source commit is created, even if that commit is never deployed.
Grant every user organization-owner access and wait for a manual command.
explain: Publish a deployment-completion event to Pub/Sub and trigger the authorized test function from it. This follows actual successful releases, unlike an independent weekly schedule that can run before deployment finishes.

stem: A racing team wants feature attributions to understand why its Vertex AI model makes particular predictions and use those findings to guide validated improvements. Which capability should it use?
options: Vertex Explainable AI.
Cloud Vision OCR as a generic explanation of every model.
Cloud Monitoring CPU charts as feature attributions.
An object lifecycle rule that retrains every model automatically.
explain: Vertex Explainable AI provides feature attributions to help investigate model behavior. It does not automatically improve predictive accuracy; use the findings to guide data and model changes and validate them on held-out data.

stem: Your team is in charge of creating a payment card data vault for card numbers used to bill tens of thousands of viewers, merchandise consumers, and season ticket holders. You need to implement a custom card tokenization service that meets the following requirements: • It must provide low latency at minimal cost. • It must be able to identify duplicate credit cards and must not store plaintext card numbers. • It should support annual key rotation. Which storage approach should you adopt for your tokenization service?
options: Persist versioned, protected token mappings in a durable store using a reviewed deterministic scheme where equality lookup is required, with separate key access and a rotation plan.
Store plaintext card numbers in application logs for deduplication.
Keep the only token mapping in an evictable cache.
Use one fixed hard-coded key forever without an authorized rotation procedure.
explain: Use a reviewed deterministic tokenization scheme when equality matching is required, and persist protected mappings in a durable store. Deterministic encryption leaks equality patterns; separate key access, version tokens, and plan rotation and migration.

stem: A recent finance audit of cloud infrastructure noted an exceptionally high number of Compute Engine instances are allocated to do video encoding and transcoding. You suspect that these Virtual Machines are zombie machines that were not deleted after their workloads completed. You need to quickly get a list of which VM instances are idle. What should you do?
options: Log into each Compute Engine instance and collect disk, CPU, memory, and network usage statistics foranalysis.
Use the gcloud compute instances list to list the virtual machine instances that have the idle: true label set.
Use the gcloud recommender command to list the idle virtual machine instances.
From the Google Console, identify which Compute Engine instances in the managed instance groups areno longer responding to health check probes.
explain: Use idle-VM recommendations from Recommender and validate business context before deletion. An arbitrary idle label or failed health check is not a reliable indicator that a VM has no useful workload.

stem: In the past, configuration errors put public IP addresses on backend servers that should not have been accessible from the Internet. You need to ensure that no one can put external IP addresses on backend Compute Engine instances and that external IP addresses can only be configured on frontend Compute Engine instances. What should you do?
options: Create an Organizational Policy with a constraint to allow external IP addresses only on the frontend Compute Engine instances.
Revoke the compute.networkAdmin role from all users in the project with front end instances.
Create an Identity and Access Management (IAM) policy that maps the IT staff to the compute.networkAdmin role for the organization.
Create a custom Identity and Access Management (IAM) role named GCE_FRONTEND with the compute.addresses.create permission.
explain: Use the compute.vmExternalIpAccess organization policy constraint with the approved instances. Network-admin permissions or address-creation permissions alone do not prevent an instance creator from attaching an external IP.

stem: A healthcare organization plans to process protected health information on Google Cloud. Which TWO actions form part of validating its service eligibility and contractual requirements?
options: Execute the applicable Business Associate Agreement.
Verify that services processing PHI are covered by the agreement and implement the required controls.
Assume every Google product is suitable for PHI because it has a Google logo.
Use a public bucket so auditors do not need authentication.
Treat a monitoring agent as a substitute for contractual review.
explain: Verify that the selected services are covered by the applicable BAA and execute the required agreement. Customer configuration, access controls, and operating procedures remain part of the compliance assessment.

stem: A healthcare application uses GKE. The team wants private worker nodes and tightly controlled control-plane access to reduce exposure. Which design is appropriate?
options: Use private nodes and restrict the control-plane endpoint to authorized private connectivity or an appropriately controlled DNS-based endpoint.
Expose every worker node directly to the public internet.
Allow anonymous access to the Kubernetes API.
Use a public control-plane endpoint with unrestricted source ranges and no additional access controls.
explain: Use private nodes and restrict control-plane access to authorized private connectivity or the appropriately controlled endpoint. Network isolation reduces exposure but must accompany workload identity, least privilege, and patch management.

stem: A game needs streaming event ingestion, managed transformations, SQL analytics, and durable raw-object retention. Which combination matches these roles?
options: Pub/Sub, Dataflow, BigQuery, and Cloud Storage.
Cloud SQL alone for ingestion, transformations, every query, and object archives.
A Compute Engine cron job, a local disk archive, and a transactional MySQL table for every analytical scan.
A single unbacked VM directory as the only data platform.
explain: Pub/Sub decouples ingestion, Dataflow transforms the stream, BigQuery serves analytics, and Cloud Storage holds durable raw data where needed. A transactional database alone is not a streaming analytical warehouse.

stem: TerramEarth plans to connect all 20 million vehicles in the field to the cloud. This increases the volume to 20 million 600 byte records a second for 40 TB an hour. How should you design the data ingestion?
options: Vehicles write data directly to GCS.
Vehicles write data directly to Pub/Sub.
Vehicles stream data directly to BigQuery.
Vehicles continue to write data using the existing system (FTP).
explain: Pub/Sub decouples vehicle event producers from downstream processing and absorbs bursts within quotas. Use authenticated ingress and batching as appropriate; implement deduplication and capacity planning rather than assuming unlimited throughput.

stem: You analyzed TerramEarth's business requirement to reduce downtime, and found that they can achieve a majority of time saving by reducing customers' wait time for parts You decided to focus on reduction of the 3 weeks aggregate reporting time Which modifications to the company's processes should you recommend?
options: Migrate from CSV to binary format, migrate from FTP to SFTP transport, and develop machine learning analysis of metrics.
Migrate from FTP to streaming transport, migrate from CSV to binary format, and develop machine learning analysis of metrics.
Increase fleet cellular connectivity to 80%, migrate from FTP to streaming transport, and develop machine learning analysis of metrics.
Migrate from FTP to SFTP transport, develop machine learning analysis of metrics, and increase dealer local inventory by a fixed factor.
explain: Increase timely connectivity and stream events instead of waiting for FTP batches, then use analytics and ML to anticipate parts demand. A file-format or encryption change alone does not remove multi-week reporting delays.

stem: Dress4Win has asked you for advice on how to migrate their on-premises MySQL deployment to the cloud. They want to minimize downtime and performance impact to their on-premises solution during the migration. Which approach should you recommend?
options: Create a dump of the on-premises MySQL master server, and then shut it down, upload it to the cloud environment, and load into a new MySQL cluster.
Setup a MySQL replica server/slave in the cloud environment, and configure it for asynchronous replication from the MySQL master server on-premises until cutover.
Create a new MySQL cluster in the cloud, configure applications to begin writing to both on-premises and cloud MySQL masters, and destroy the original cluster at cutover.
Create a dump of the MySQL replica server into the cloud environment, load it into: Firestore in Datastore mode, and configure applications to read/write to Firestore in Datastore mode at cutover.
explain: Replicate from the source to the destination, validate consistency, then cut over once replication catches up. Database Migration Service can manage supported migrations; a long offline dump stops writes for much longer.

stem: You want to store critical business information in Cloud Storage buckets. The information is regularly changed but previous versions need to be referenced on a regular basis. You want to ensure that there is a record of all changes to any information in these buckets. You want to ensure that accidental edits or deletions can be easily roiled back. Which feature should you enable?
options: Enable Object Versioning with suitable lifecycle and soft-delete policies for noncurrent generations.
Use only a notification and assume it retains the prior object contents.
Disable all recovery copies to reduce storage charges.
Use a bucket label as a replacement for version history.
explain: Object Versioning retains noncurrent object generations so previous values can be restored. Configure appropriate lifecycle and soft-delete settings; lifecycle deletion and bucket retention serve different purposes.

stem: You have developed an application using Vertex AI that recognizes famous paintings from uploaded images. You want to test the application and allow specific people to upload images for the next 24 hours. Not all users have a Google Account. How should you have users upload images?
options: Have users upload the images to Cloud Storag Protect the bucket with a passwordthat expires after 24 hours.
Have users upload the images to Cloud Storage using a signed URL that expires after 24 hours.
Create an App Engine web application where users can upload image Configure App Engine to disable the application after 24 hour Authenticate users via Cloud Identity.
Create an App Engine web application where users can upload images for the next 24 hour Authenticate users via Cloud Identity.
explain: Issue short-lived upload authorization, such as a signed URL for a supported upload method or a signed POST policy. The user needs no Google account, and the backend must enforce file constraints and expiry.

stem: Your company has a Google Workspace account and Google Cloud Organization Some developers in the company have created Google Cloud projects outside of the Google Cloud Organization You want to create an Organization structure that allows developers to create projects, but prevents them from modifying production projects You want to manage policies for all projects centrally and be able to set more restrictive policies for production projects You want to minimize disruption to users and developers when business needs change in the future You want to follow Google-recommended practices How should you design the Organization structure?
options: Use Development and Production folders; grant developers project-creation permissions only in Development and apply baseline policies at the organization.
Create every development project outside the organization so no guardrails apply.
Grant all developers Owner at the organization and try to revoke it with a Viewer grant on Production.
Use one ungoverned shared project for all environments.
explain: Create separate development and production folders and scope developer project-creation rights to development. Organization policies establish the baseline, and production-folder policies add controls without opening production administration.

stem: You have a Python web application with many dependencies that requires 0.1 CPU cores and 128 MB of memory to operate in production. You want to monitor and maximize machine utilization. You also to reliably deploy new versions of the application. Which set of steps should you take?
options: Build an immutable, versioned container, test it in staging, and promote the same digest to production with explicit resource requests.
Use only a mutable latest tag and restart pods to deploy unknown changes.
Install unpinned dependencies manually on each node.
Keep the production artifact different from the one tested in staging.
explain: Build a versioned image with all dependencies, test it in staging, then promote the same immutable artifact. Small resource requests improve packing; mutable latest tags and restarts do not create an auditable release process.

stem: A development manager is building a new application He asks you to review his requirements and identify what cloud technologies he can use to meet them. The application must * 1. Be based on open-source technology for cloud portability * 2. Dynamically scale compute capacity based on demand * 3. Support continuous software delivery * 4. Run multiple segregated copies of the same application stack * 5. Deploy application bundles using dynamic templates * 6. Route network traffic to specific services based on URL Which combination of technologies will meet all of his requirements?
options: GKE, Jenkins, and Helm.
GKE and a load balancer, with no build or release tooling.
Compute Engine and Infrastructure Manager without an application orchestration or release design.
Manually configured Compute Engine VMs, a CI server, and one load balancer without container orchestration.
explain: Kubernetes, an open CI system, and Helm support portable application delivery with declarative packaging. Configure autoscaling explicitly; choosing an open-source component does not by itself make the complete architecture portable.

stem: A company accesses BigQuery from on-premises over private hybrid connectivity. It wants to reduce exfiltration risk from compromised credentials while retaining authorized analytics. What should it configure?
options: A VPC Service Controls perimeter, appropriate ingress and egress policies, and the documented private Google API access path.
Only a VPN tunnel, assuming private transport prevents all data exfiltration.
Only a project label indicating that the data is private.
An external IP on every analyst workstation.
explain: VPC Service Controls constrains data movement across supported service perimeters. Private Google Access supplies a private API path, while IAM remains necessary; private connectivity alone does not stop authorized credentials being misused.

stem: You are tasked with building an online analytical processing (OLAP) marketing analytics and reporting tool. This requires a relational database that can operate on hundreds of terabytes of data. What is the Google recommended tool for such applications?
options: Cloud Spanner, because it is globally distributed
Cloud SQL, because it is a fully managed relational database
Cloud Firestore, because it offers real-time synchronization across devices
BigQuery, because it is designed for large-scale processing of tabular data
explain: BigQuery is designed for large-scale analytical SQL over hundreds of terabytes. Spanner is for scalable transactional relational workloads; global distribution alone is not the right reason to choose an OLAP engine.

stem: A read-heavy application repeatedly issues identical database queries. It can tolerate a short, defined staleness window. Which cache design reduces database load safely?
options: Use cache-aside with query- and authorization-specific keys, bounded TTLs, and defined invalidation rules.
Store every query result under one shared cache key.
Cache all users' private results together without authorization checks.
Populate the cache once during deployment and retain results indefinitely despite the freshness requirement.
explain: Check a bounded-TTL cache using a key derived from the query and relevant authorization context, then populate it on a miss. A single shared key for all queries returns incorrect results; plan invalidation to meet freshness requirements.

stem: You want to optimize the performance of an accurate, real-time, weather-charting application. The data comes from 50,000 sensors sending 10 readings a second, in the format of a timestamp and sensor reading. Where should you store the data?
options: BigQuery
Cloud SQL
Bigtable
Cloud Storage
explain: Bigtable supports high write rates and low-latency key-range reads for sensor data. Design distributed row keys and retention policies; object storage is not a low-latency per-sensor database.

stem: Your company is using Google Cloud. You have two folders under the Organization: Finance and Shopping. The members of the development team are in a Google Group. The development team group has been assigned the Project Owner role on the Organization. You want to prevent the development team from creating resources in projects in the Finance folder. What should you do?
options: Remove the organization-wide Owner grant and assign only the required permissions under Shopping.
Add Viewer on Finance while leaving inherited Owner unchanged.
Assign the developers Viewer on Finance and leave the organization-level Owner grant in place.
Create another broad organization Owner grant.
explain: Remove the organization-wide Owner grant and reassign only the required scope under Shopping. A Viewer grant on Finance does not cancel inherited Owner permissions.

stem: A Python container build copies the entire source tree before installing dependencies. Every source change invalidates the dependency layer, and the base image contains unnecessary tools. Which TWO changes improve build and deployment speed while keeping required functionality?
options: Use a compatible slim runtime base image.
Copy dependency manifests and install dependencies before copying frequently changed source.
Remove required dependencies from the manifest.
Delete Python from the final image even though the application needs it.
Use a mutable latest tag as the only release identifier.
explain: Install stable dependencies before copying frequently changed source, and choose a smaller compatible runtime base. This reuses build layers and reduces image downloads while preserving application requirements.

stem: A Java application on a supported runtime fails at startup with ClassNotFoundException for a required third-party class. The application artifact does not include that dependency. What should the developer do?
options: Package the missing runtime dependency correctly, verify version compatibility, and redeploy.
Digitally sign every JAR and leave the dependency absent.
Change every SHA-256 hash to MD5.
Increase VM disk size without changing the artifact.
explain: Use the actual exception to fix a missing dependency or unsupported runtime API. Supply required JARs and use a supported runtime or container; blanket JAR signing or changing hash algorithms is not a general deployment fix.

stem: You want to allow your operations learn to store togs from all the production protects in your Organization, without during logs from other projects All of the production projects are contained in a folder. You want to ensure that all logs for existing and new production projects are captured automatically. What should you do?
options: Create an aggregated sink on the Production folder including child projects, routed to the central destination.
Configure only one current project and assume future projects are included.
Create a sink at the organization root without filtering and claim no development logs are captured.
Copy logs manually once a year.
explain: Create an aggregated sink at the production folder with child inclusion and a central destination. New child projects are covered automatically without exporting unrelated development logs.

stem: You are running a cluster on Kubernetes Engine to serve a web application. Users are reporting that a specific part of the application is not responding anymore. You notice that all pods of your deployment keep restarting after 2 seconds. The application writes logs to standard output. You want to inspect the logs to find the cause of the issue. Which approach can you take?
options: Review the Cloud Operations logs for each Compute Engine instance that is serving as a node in the cluster.
Review the Cloud Operations logs for the specific Kubernetes Engine container that is serving the unresponsive part of the application.
Connect to the cluster using gcloud credentials and connect to a container in one of the pods to read the logs.
Review the Serial Port logs for each Compute Engine instance that is serving as a node in the cluster.
explain: Inspect the affected container's centrally collected logs or kubectl logs --previous. Node and serial logs are useful for infrastructure failures but are not the primary source for an application's stdout exception.

stem: After a new Linux kernel module is installed on Compute Engine batch VMs, some fail during a nightly job. Which THREE sources help correlate guest-level failures and resource conditions?
options: Use Cloud Logging to search for the module log entries.
Read the debug GCE Activity log using the API or Cloud Console.
Use gcloud or Cloud Console to connect to the serial console and observe the logs.
Identify whether a live migration event of the failed server occurred, using in the activity log.
Adjust the Cloud Operations timeline to match the failure time, and observe the batch server metrics.
Export a debug VM into an image, and run the image on a local server where kernel log messages will be displayed on the native screen.
explain: Correlate guest kernel logs, serial-console output, and resource metrics around the failure. Preserve a snapshot before intrusive repair; administrative audit events do not contain guest kernel stack traces.

stem: You have deployed an application to Kubernetes Engine, and are using the Cloud SQL proxy container to make the Cloud SQL database available to the services running on Kubernetes. You are notified that the application is reporting database connection issues. Your company policies require a post- mortem. What should you do?
options: Inspect the application, Cloud SQL Auth Proxy, GKE, and Cloud SQL logs, then validate identity and connectivity.
Restore a backup immediately without checking whether data is damaged.
Grant Cloud Build Editor and assume that authorizes database connections.
Delete every pod and all diagnostic logs before investigating.
explain: Inspect application, Cloud SQL Auth Proxy, GKE, and Cloud SQL logs before restarting or restoring anything. Validate the proxy identity's Cloud SQL Client permissions and the configured network path.

stem: BigQuery analysts use private hybrid connectivity from on-premises. The organization wants to constrain supported API data movement even if a credential is compromised. What should it deploy?
options: VPC Service Controls with appropriate access rules and Private Google Access for on-premises hosts.
A service-account key shared by all analysts.
Only private transport with no data perimeter or IAM review.
Add a private IP route only and assume it limits which external projects may receive data.
explain: Use a VPC Service Controls perimeter and the documented private Google API access path from on-premises. Job permissions and object-read permissions alone cannot constrain where an authorized caller sends data.

stem: Developers must stage a Cloud Run release, but an operations team must independently approve promotion to production. How should the team separate these duties?
options: Use Cloud Deploy approval and scoped IAM, promoting an immutable artifact tested in the staging target.
Give all developers unrestricted production administration.
Require the operations team to rebuild source manually after every test.
Use one shared owner account for build, approval, and deployment.
explain: Use separately deployable versions and IAM so developers stage a release while operators promote it. Cloud Run and Cloud Deploy can implement this with explicit approval and immutable artifacts.

stem: Google Cloud resources are managed hierarchically using organization, folders, and projects. When Cloud Identity and Access Management (IAM) policies exist at these different levels, what is the effective policy at a particular node of the hierarchy?
options: The effective policy is determined only by the policy set at the node
The effective policy is the policy set at the node and restricted by the policies of its ancestors
The effective policy is the union of the policy set at the node and policies inherited from its ancestors
The effective policy is the intersection of the policy set at the node and policies inherited from its ancestors
explain: Allow-policy grants are additive down the resource hierarchy. Child Viewer grants do not restrict an inherited Owner grant; separately evaluate deny policies, conditions, and other access restrictions.

stem: Your company is running a stateless application on a Compute Engine instance. The application is used heavily during regular business hours and lightly outside of business hours. Users are reporting that the application is slow during peak hours. You need to optimize the application’s performance. What should you do?
options: Create a custom image, reference it in an instance template, and create an autoscaled managed instance group behind a load balancer.
Use a disk snapshot alone as a managed instance group template.
Keep one fixed-size VM and manually terminate traffic at peak hours.
Create several independent VMs with no load balancer, instance template, or scaling policy.
explain: Create a reusable image, reference it in an instance template, and create an autoscaled managed instance group behind a load balancer. A snapshot is a disk backup, not an instance template or autoscaling policy.

stem: As part of implementing their disaster recovery plan, your company is trying to replicate their production MySQL database from their private data center to their Google Cloud project using a Google Cloud VPN connection. They are experiencing latency issues and a small amount of packet loss that is disrupting the replication. What should they do?
options: Configure their replication to use UDP.
Configure a Google Cloud Dedicated Interconnect.
Restore their database daily using Cloud SQL.
Add additional VPN connections and load balance them.
Send the replicated transaction to Pub/Sub.
explain: A suitably redundant Interconnect design offers predictable private bandwidth for substantial replication traffic. First measure packet loss, MTU, throughput, and latency; switching database replication to UDP is not a valid fix.

stem: You need to evaluate your team readiness for a new Google Cloud project. You must perform the evaluation and create a skills gap plan incorporates the business goal of cost optimization. Your team has deployed two Google Cloud projects successfully to date. What should you do?
options: Assess role-specific gaps and fund a training and certification roadmap tied to project milestones.
Set a deadline without assessing skills.
Hire consultants indefinitely without transferring knowledge.
Cancel all cost training because the team has completed two projects.
explain: Assess role-specific gaps and create a funded training and certification roadmap aligned to delivery milestones. Building internal capability reduces recurring dependence on outside consultants; deadlines alone do not close skills gaps.

stem: You are designing a Data Warehouse on Google Cloud and want to store sensitive data in BigQuery. Your company requires you to generate encryption keys outside of Google Cloud. You need to implement a solution. What should you do?
options: Import externally generated key material into Cloud KMS and configure BigQuery customer-managed encryption with the required service-agent permissions.
Generate the key inside Cloud KMS despite the external-generation requirement.
Pass a Cloud Storage customer-supplied key directly as a BigQuery dataset property.
Configure a default Cloud Storage key and assume it also applies to unrelated BigQuery datasets.
explain: Import externally generated key material into Cloud KMS and configure BigQuery CMEK with that key. BigQuery uses CMEK rather than Cloud Storage-style customer-supplied encryption keys; grant the BigQuery service agent key access.

stem: You are using a single Cloud SQL instance to serve your application from a specific zone. You want to introduce high availability. What should you do?
options: Enable regional Cloud SQL high availability with a standby in another zone of the same region.
Create only an asynchronous read replica in another region and call it automatic regional HA.
Create two unrelated databases with no replication.
Place the only database and backup in one local SSD volume.
explain: Configure regional Cloud SQL HA with a standby in another zone of the same region. A cross-region read replica is asynchronous disaster-recovery capacity and does not substitute for automatic regional HA.

stem: Your company has an application running on a deployment in a GKE cluster. You have a separate cluster for development, staging and production. You have discovered that the team is able to deploy a Docker image to the production cluster without first testing the deployment in development and then staging. You want to allow the team to have autonomy but want to prevent this from happening. You want a Google Cloud solution that can be implemented quickly with minimal effort. What should you do?
options: Enforce Binary Authorization policies with attestations created after required pipeline test stages.
Use only a written instruction asking developers to test first.
Use only a container lifecycle hook as the approval boundary.
Let every production user change the trusted attestor keys.
explain: Create attestations after required pipeline tests and enforce environment-specific Binary Authorization policies. A lifecycle hook or written policy cannot reliably prevent an unapproved image from being admitted.

stem: Your company is forecasting a sharp increase in the number and size of Apache Spark and Hadoop jobs being run on your local datacenter You want to utilize the cloud to help you scale this upcoming demand with the least amount of operations work and code change. Which product should you use?
options: Dataflow
Managed Service for Apache Spark.
Compute Engine
Google Kubernetes Engine
explain: Managed Service for Apache Spark runs existing Spark and Hadoop workloads with fewer infrastructure changes than a Beam rewrite. Use the execution mode and cluster lifecycle that fit the jobs' dependencies.

stem: A 4 TB on-premises PostgreSQL database has frequent large updates. Its cloud replica needs private address connectivity, predictable high bandwidth, and a redundant network design. Which approach is most suitable?
options: Redundant Dedicated or Partner Interconnect with appropriate attachments and routing.
One public NAT gateway pretending to be private database replication.
An unencrypted public FTP connection.
A single unmanaged VPN VM with no redundancy or throughput assessment.
explain: Dedicated or Partner Interconnect provides private connectivity and suitable throughput for large, frequently updated replicas. Design redundant attachments and monitor replication lag; a single link remains a failure domain.

stem: You have an application that will run on Compute Engine. You need to design an architecture that takes into account a disaster recovery plan that requires your application to fail over to another region in case of a regional outage. What should you do?
options: Deploy managed instance groups in two regions behind a global external Application Load Balancer, with appropriate replicated state and tested failover.
Deploy two instances in the same zone and call them independent regions.
Deploy a second load balancer in another region while keeping all compute and data in the first region.
Keep a single VM with local-only data and no recovery process.
explain: Deploy regional instance groups across two regions behind a global external Application Load Balancer and replicate state appropriately. Health-based routing moves traffic, but compute redundancy alone does not replicate application data.

stem: An application lets millions of users upload images and share them with selected users. The team wants managed container hosting with minimal infrastructure management. Which compute platform is a good fit?
options: Cloud Run with Cloud Storage and a suitable managed metadata database.
A single manually operated VM with images only on local disk.
A self-managed Kubernetes control plane solely to host one stateless upload API.
A permanent user desktop acting as the public web server.
explain: Cloud Run provides managed container hosting and automatic scaling so developers can focus on application code. Store uploaded objects in Cloud Storage and use an external database rather than local ephemeral files.

stem: You want to establish a Compute Engine application in a single VPC across two regions. The application must communicate over VPN to an on-premises network. How should you deploy the VPN?
options: Deploy regional HA VPN gateways with the required redundant tunnels and configure dynamic routing for cross-region reachability.
Create a global VPN gateway because a VPC is global.
Use VPC Network Peering directly to an on-premises physical network.
Configure only one tunnel in one region and omit the required cross-region dynamic routing design.
explain: Cloud VPN gateways are regional. Deploy redundant regional gateways and configure dynamic routing as required for reachability across the VPC; a global VPC does not imply a global VPN gateway.

stem: Your company wants to try out the cloud with low risk. They want to archive approximately 100 TB of their log data to the cloud and test the analytics features available to them there, while also retaining that data as a long-term disaster recovery backup. Which two steps should they take?
options: Load logs into BigQuery.
Load logs into Cloud SQL.
Import logs into Cloud Operations.
Insert logs into Bigtable.
Upload log files into Cloud Storage.
explain: Keep a durable Cloud Storage archive and load or expose the data to BigQuery for SQL analysis. Operational log tooling and transactional databases are not replacements for both cheap bulk retention and analytical queries.

stem: Your company provides a recommendation engine for retail customers. You are providing retail customers with an API where they can submit a user ID and the API returns a list of recommendations for that user. You are responsible for the API lifecycle and want to ensure stability for your customers in case the API makes backward-incompatible changes. You want to follow Google-recommended practices. What should you do?
options: Introduce a new version for backward-incompatible changes and maintain a documented migration period for existing clients.
Replace the old version's behavior silently under the same contract.
Rename the old API to DEPRECATED and immediately remove it without notice.
Version APIs only by the time of day so clients cannot pin behavior.
explain: Introduce a new API version for backward-incompatible changes and keep the existing version available during a documented migration period. Renaming the old version or silently replacing its behavior breaks clients.

stem: You have deployed several instances on Compute Engine. As a security requirement, instances cannot have a public IP address. There is no VPN connection between Google Cloud and your office, and you need to connect via SSH into a specific machine without violating the security requirements. What should you do?
options: Use IAP TCP forwarding with IAP-secured Tunnel User and appropriate OS Login permissions.
SSH inbound through Cloud NAT.
Create an unauthenticated public proxy to every backend VM.
Temporarily expose all SSH ports to 0.0.0.0/0.
explain: Use IAP TCP forwarding, the IAP-secured Tunnel User role, and OS Login or appropriately managed SSH access. Cloud NAT permits outbound connections; it does not accept inbound SSH sessions.

stem: Your company is using BigQuery as its enterprise data warehouse. Data is distributed over several Google Cloud projects. All queries on BigQuery need to be billed on a single project. You want to make sure that no query costs are incurred on the projects that contain the data. Users should be able to query the datasets, but not edit them. How should you configure users’ access roles?
options: Grant BigQuery Job User on the billing project and Data Viewer on the source datasets, and submit jobs in the billing project.
Grant Job User on every data project and assume all jobs are billed centrally.
Grant BigQuery Data Viewer on the billing project but Job User only on the data projects.
Copy every dataset into the billing project before every query.
explain: Grant BigQuery Job User on the query billing project and Data Viewer on source datasets. Run jobs in the billing project; read permission on a data project need not include job-creation permission there.

stem: BigQuery source tables contain PII accessible only to compliance staff. Analysts need non-PII columns without direct access to the source. What is the simplest controlled sharing pattern?
options: Create authorized views excluding PII in a separate dataset and grant analysts access to that dataset, not the source tables.
Give analysts source-table access and ask them not to select sensitive columns.
Put PII in a column whose name begins with underscore.
Share source-owner credentials with the analysts.
explain: Place a view excluding sensitive columns in a separate dataset, authorize it on the source dataset, and grant analysts access only to the view dataset. Granting direct source-table access bypasses the intended restriction.

stem: Your company's test suite is a custom C++ application that runs tests throughout each day on Linux virtual machines. The full test suite takes several hours to complete, running on a limited number of on premises servers reserved for testing. Your company wants to move the testing infrastructure to the cloud, to reduce the amount of time it takes to fully test a change to the system, while changing the tests as little as possible. Which cloud infrastructure should you recommend?
options: Use managed instance groups or Batch with partitioned parallel test tasks and centralized result collection.
Use a load balancer alone and assume it partitions the entire test suite.
Use one fixed on-premises machine forever regardless of queue depth.
Move the same serial test runner to one fixed VM and do not partition or parallelize tests.
explain: Use managed instance groups or Batch to execute parallel Linux test work and release idle compute. A load balancer alone does not divide a test suite; design task partitioning and result collection explicitly.

stem: A team is starting new analytical pipelines that need both batch and streaming execution using a unified programming model with minimal infrastructure administration. Which service should it evaluate?
options: Dataflow with Apache Beam.
A manually managed permanent Hadoop cluster solely because the data is analytical.
Cloud SQL as a generic replacement for all streaming transformations.
A single local CSV editor for all streaming events.
explain: Dataflow runs Apache Beam pipelines for both bounded and unbounded data with managed scaling. Dataproc is useful for existing Spark/Hadoop ecosystems, but there is no such compatibility requirement here.

stem: A team has Google Groups representing its users. It needs straightforward Cloud Storage access control, with no requirement to supply or manage encryption keys. What should it use?
options: Assign suitable predefined storage roles to groups and use default encryption at rest unless requirements demand a different key model.
Build a custom role for every user even when predefined roles meet the requirement.
Store the customer-supplied encryption key in object metadata so every reader can retrieve it.
Disable encryption at rest to simplify role management.
explain: Assign suitable predefined roles to groups and use default encryption at rest unless requirements demand customer-managed keys. Custom roles and customer-supplied keys add maintenance without automatically improving the required control.

stem: Raw telemetry must remain readily available for 30 days, then retained with infrequent access until it is deleted after 365 days. Which lifecycle policy satisfies this pattern while lowering storage cost?
options: Create a Cloud Storage lifecycle rule with Age: “30”, Storage Class: “Standard”, and Action: “Set to Coldline”, and create a second GCS life-cycle rule with Age: “365”, Storage Class: “Coldline”, and Action: “Delete”.

Create a Cloud Storage lifecycle rule with Age: “30”, Storage Class: “Coldline”, and Action: “Set to Nearline”, and create a second GCS life-cycle rule with Age: “91”, Storage Class: “Coldline”, and Action: “Set to Nearline”.

Create a Cloud Storage lifecycle rule with Age: “90”, Storage Class: “Standard”, and Action: “Set to Nearline”, and create a second GCS life-cycle rule with Age: “91”, Storage Class: “Nearline”, and Action: “Set to Coldline”.

Create a Cloud Storage lifecycle rule with Age: “30”, Storage Class: “Standard”, and Action: “Set to Coldline”, and create a second GCS life-cycle rule with Age: “365”, Storage Class: “Nearline”, and Action: “Delete”.
explain: Use lifecycle transitions for colder access and delete objects after the required one-year period. Match the rule's storage-class condition to the class actually in use, and account for minimum storage-duration charges.

stem: Mountkirk Games wants you to secure the connectivity from the new gaming application platform to Google Cloud. You want to streamline the process and follow Google-recommended practices. What should you do?
options: Use Workload Identity Federation for GKE with least-privilege IAM for the application.
Distribute one service account private key to every pod.
Assume base64-encoded Kubernetes Secrets are encryption.
Grant Editor to the node service account and let every pod inherit that broad identity.
explain: Use Workload Identity Federation for GKE with narrowly scoped IAM grants. Base64-encoded Kubernetes Secrets are not encryption and distributing service account JSON keys increases credential exposure.

stem: A game serves active player requests that cannot tolerate sudden worker preemption. Demand varies, and the team needs automatic capacity changes and regional redundancy. Which compute design is appropriate?
options: Non-interruptible serving capacity across zones with autoscaling and a load balancer appropriate to the game protocol.
Only Spot VMs with no session recovery or replacement capacity.
One manually scaled instance with no load balancer.
A nightly offline batch cluster instead of online game servers.
explain: Use healthy non-interruptible serving capacity across zones with autoscaling and the load balancer matching the protocol. Spot capacity fits tolerant batch work, not an assumption of uninterrupted player sessions.

stem: A racing team keeps historical telemetry and mainly analyzes or trains on a selected season. It needs an analytical store that scales and supports evolving schemas. Which approach is appropriate?
options: BigQuery with suitable time partitioning and clustering, plus raw history in Cloud Storage as needed.
A separate always-on Cloud SQL instance for every race lap.
Store all seasons as unpartitioned large JSON objects in a transactional database and scan them for every report.
Use a transactional database solely because its name includes global distribution.
explain: BigQuery partitioning and clustering prune data for season-specific training and analysis, while Cloud Storage retains raw history where appropriate. Large transactional Spanner instances are not required just to retain analytical telemetry.

stem: A service behind an external Application Load Balancer must accept requests only from a supported CDN provider IP list. Which control should be applied at the load balancer?
options: A Cloud Armor security policy using the provider's supported named IP-list expression, with an appropriate default-deny policy.
Only a network tag named after the CDN provider.
A Cloud NAT rule for unsolicited inbound HTTPS.
An object lifecycle rule on the backend bucket.
explain: Apply a Cloud Armor security policy to the external Application Load Balancer using the supported named IP-list expression for the CDN. VPC firewall commands do not configure the load balancer's layer-7 policy.

stem: In the past, configuration errors put public IP addresses on backend servers that should not have been accessible from the Internet. You need to ensure that no one can put external IP addresses on backend Compute Engine instances and that external IP addresses can only be configured on frontend Compute Engine instances. What should you do?
options: Create an Organizational Policy with a constraint to allow external IP addresses only on the frontend Compute Engine instances.
Revoke the compute.networkAdmin role from all users in the project with front end instances.
Create an Identity and Access Management (IAM) policy that maps the IT staff to the compute.networkAdmin role for the organization.
Create a custom Identity and Access Management (IAM) role named GCE_FRONTEND with the compute.addresses.create permission.
explain: Enforce the external-IP organization policy with approved instance values. Changing IAM for network administrators alone does not express a resource-level allowlist for VM external addresses.

stem: A business-critical workload has one private Interconnect connection from its data center to Google Cloud. Public-internet transport is not allowed. What change addresses the connection's single point of failure?
options: Add redundant Interconnect connectivity across the required independent failure domains.
Only increase bandwidth on the existing physical connection.
Replace private connectivity with public peering.
Add an internet-based VPN and assume it never traverses the internet.
explain: Add a redundant Interconnect connection with the appropriate independent failure domains. More bandwidth on the existing link does not remove its single point of failure; public peering does not provide the same private VPC path.

stem: A data center has one Interconnect connection to Google Cloud. Its servers use private addresses, and policy forbids production traffic from traversing the public internet. Which improvement adds private network redundancy?
options: Add redundant Interconnect connectivity in the appropriate independent failure domains and validate failover.
Only increase the bandwidth of the single connection.
Replace the private path with public internet peering.
Assume three internet VPNs satisfy a policy forbidding internet transit.
explain: Design redundant Interconnect connections and attachments across the documented failure domains. A bandwidth upgrade alone does not add redundancy, and VPN traverses the internet even though its traffic is encrypted.

stem: A team needs separate development, staging, and production administration. Developers can share development resources but cannot administer staging or production. Staging calls a limited production API. Which boundary should it use?
options: Separate projects per environment, scoped IAM, and explicit authorized service connectivity.
One subnet per environment with organization-owner permissions for every developer.
One shared Owner account across all environments.
No IAM restrictions because containers provide all administrative isolation.
explain: Use separate development, staging, and production projects, with explicit IAM and service connectivity for the required cross-environment access. Subnets alone are not an administrative or deployment boundary.

stem: A game has a sharp traffic increase. Its autoscaling group is at capacity and users see 503 responses. The application is healthy but scale-out requests fail. What should operators inspect first?
options: Project quota, autoscaler events, and capacity constraints.
Immediately rewrite database indexes without first inspecting the failed scale-out requests.
Increase log-retention duration before investigating why instance creation fails.
Change the load-balancer hostname while leaving failed provisioning requests unresolved.
explain: Check quota and autoscaler events when demand exceeds capacity and scaling fails. Healthy application code cannot create more instances after a quota ceiling is reached.

stem: A vehicle fleet needs centralized queries over telemetry and predictive-maintenance model training. Which architecture separates event ingestion, stream processing, analytical queries, and model development?
options: Pub/Sub to Dataflow to BigQuery, with Vertex AI for model training and Cloud Storage for raw history.
Write directly to one Cloud SQL instance and use operational transaction queries as the entire fleet analytics and training platform.
Send events only to Cloud Logging and use log-based alerts as the model-training store.
Run periodic FTP transfers to one VM and process all fleet data in its memory with no durable archive.
explain: Use Pub/Sub for ingestion, Dataflow for processing, BigQuery for centralized analysis, and Vertex AI for model development. Keep Cloud Storage raw history where needed; an analytical workflow should not query every individual vehicle directly.

stem: Vehicles will upload compressed historical telemetry for model training next year. The data will rarely be read before then. Which approach avoids unnecessary always-on processing costs?
options: Batch and compress on the vehicle and store uploads in an appropriate cold Cloud Storage class.
Maintain a continuously running streaming database only to archive untouched files.
Store the only copy on an unbacked local SSD.
Stream all data into a continuously running low-latency serving cluster despite having no current query requirement.
explain: Compress and batch data locally and place rarely read historical objects in an appropriate cold Cloud Storage class. A continuously running streaming database is unnecessary when the data will only be used next year.

stem: Which of TerramEarth's legacy enterprise processes will experience significant change as a result of increased Google Cloud adoption.
options: Opex/capex allocation, LAN changes, capacity planning
Capacity planning, TCO calculations, opex/capex allocation
Capacity planning, utilization measurement, data center expansion
Data Center expansion, TCO calculations, utilization measurement
explain: Elastic capacity and consumption pricing change capacity planning, total-cost modeling, and capital-versus-operating-expense allocation. Treat accounting classification as an organizational decision, and track actual utilization and commitments.

stem: A manufacturer needs a partner API with managed authentication and quotas. Developers should focus on business logic instead of writing an API gateway framework. Which approach is appropriate?
options: Run business logic on Cloud Run and use API Gateway or Apigee as appropriate for API management requirements.
Build a custom authentication protocol and distribute shared administrator passwords.
Expose a database directly to every external partner.
Use VPC firewall rules alone to implement end-user API quotas and delegated application authorization.
explain: Use a supported application runtime with managed API authentication, quotas, and lifecycle tooling such as Apigee or API Gateway. Focus the interface on authorized partners rather than writing a custom API framework from scratch.

stem: As part of their new application experience, Dress4Win allows customers to upload images of themselves. The customer has exclusive control over who may view these images. Customers should be able to upload images with minimal latency and also be shown their images quickly on the main application page when they log in. Which configuration should Dress4Win use?
options: Store image objects in Cloud Storage and ownership/visibility metadata in Firestore, enforcing authorization before issuing access.
Store all images only in one web server's temporary directory.
Put a customer ID in object metadata and assume this alone prevents unauthorized reads.
Grant every authenticated customer public-bucket administration.
explain: Store images in Cloud Storage and searchable ownership/visibility metadata in Firestore. Enforce authorization before issuing short-lived access; metadata containing a customer ID is not itself an access-control mechanism.

stem: Dress4win has end to end tests covering 100% of their endpoints. They want to ensure that the move of cloud does not introduce any new bugs. Which additional testing methods should the developers employ to prevent an outage?
options: Add unit tests and representative production-scale load tests in staging.
Use an interactive debugger as the only pre-release quality check.
Remove end-to-end tests after moving to the cloud.
Wait for a production outage to learn the capacity limit.
explain: Unit tests and production-scale load tests expose component regressions and capacity problems. A debugger is diagnostic tooling, not a substitute for pre-release testing under expected load.

stem: The current Dress4win system architecture has high latency to some customers because it is located in one data center. As of a future evaluation and optimizing for performance in the cloud, Dresss4win wants to distribute it's system architecture to multiple locations when Google cloud platform. Which approach should they use?
options: Use regional managed instance groups in multiple regions behind a global external Application Load Balancer.
Use one regional group and assume its instances automatically span all continents.
Route every request through a manual proxy in the original distant data center.
Change DNS names without placing compute nearer users.
explain: Serve traffic from regional managed instance groups in multiple regions behind a global external Application Load Balancer. Scale each region based on demand; a regional group alone does not span regions.

stem: You are responsible for the Google Cloud environment in your company Multiple departments need access to their own projects and the members within each department will have the same project responsibilities You want to structure your Google Cloud environment for minimal maintenance and maximum overview of 1AM permissions as each department's projects start and end You want to follow Google-recommended practices What should you do?
options: Use a Google Group and folder for each department, with scoped folder-level roles inherited by its projects.
Grant every individual Owner at the organization.
Maintain unrelated manual permissions for every user on every resource.
Use one shared service account for all department members rather than group-based human access.
explain: Manage department membership through Google Groups, place projects in department folders, and grant scoped roles to the groups. This reduces per-user and per-project policy maintenance.

stem: Your company has a networking team and a development team. The development team runs applications on Compute Engine instances that contain sensitive data. The development team requires administrative permissions for Compute Engine. Your company requires all network resources to be managed by the networking team. The development team does not want the networking team to have access to the sensitive data on the instances. What should you do?
options: * 1. Create a project with a standalone VPC and assign the Network Admin role to the networking team.* 2. Create a second project with a standalone VPC and assign the Compute Admin role to the development team.* 3. Use Cloud VPN to join the two VPCs.
* 1. Create a project with a standalone Virtual Private Cloud (VPC), assign the Network Admin role to the networking team, and assign the Compute Admin role to the development team.

* 1. Create a project with a Shared VPC and assign the Network Admin role to the networking team.* 2. Create a second project without a VPC, configure it as a Shared VPC service project,and assign the Compute Admin role to the development team.

* 1. Create a project with a standalone VPC and assign the Network Admin role to the networking team.* 2. Create a second project with a standalone VPC and assign the Compute Admin role to the development team.* 3. Use VPC Peering to join the two VPCs.
explain: Use a Shared VPC host project for the network team and service projects for application teams. Scope application compute permissions so they cannot administer the centrally owned network.

stem: Your company recently acquired a company that has infrastructure in Google Cloud. Each company has its own Google Cloud organization Each company is using a Shared Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) to provide network connectivity tor its applications Some of the subnets used by both companies overlap In order for both businesses to integrate, the applications need to have private network connectivity. These applications are not on overlapping subnets. You want to provide connectivity with minimal re-engineering. What should you do?
options: Renumber overlapping networks for routed connectivity, or use Private Service Connect for supported service-level access.
Peer overlapping VPC ranges without any address or service design changes.
Use ordinary VPN routing and assume identical destination ranges become distinguishable.
Open firewall ingress broadly and assume it rewrites destination addresses.
explain: Renumber overlapping ranges for general routed connectivity, or expose specific services through Private Service Connect where supported. Peering and ordinary VPN routes cannot distinguish identical destination ranges.

stem: Your organization wants to control IAM policies for different departments independently, but centrally. Which approach should you take?
options: Multiple Organizations with multiple Folders
Create a different organization for every department.
Use one organization with department folders and scoped delegated administration.
Place every project directly under the organization and delegate only through a shared owner account.
explain: Use one organization with departmental folders and delegated administration at the folder level. Multiple organizations add unnecessary identity and governance boundaries for this requirement.

stem: Your company is planning to perform a lift and shift migration of their Linux RHEL 6.5+ virtual machines. The virtual machines are running in an on-premises VMware environment. You want to migrate them to Compute Engine following Google- recommended practices. What should you do?
options: Assess dependencies, plan migration waves and rollback, then use Migrate to Virtual Machines for supported sources.
Copy every disk independently without application discovery.
Migrate only one random VM and assume all dependencies follow.
Keep unsupported OS images indefinitely without a support and upgrade plan.
explain: Assess workload dependencies, define migration waves and a rollback plan, then use Migrate to Virtual Machines for supported sources. Importing every disk independently skips discovery and coordinated cutover planning.

stem: Your company is designing its data lake on Google Cloud and wants to develop different ingestion pipelines to collect unstructured data from different sources. After the data is stored in Google Cloud, it will be processed in several data pipelines to build a recommendation engine for end users on the website. The structure of the data retrieved from the source systems can change at any time. The data must be stored exactly as it was retrieved for reprocessing purposes in case the data structure is incompatible with the current processing pipelines. You need to design an architecture to support the use case after you retrieve the data. What should you do?
options: Land raw data in Cloud Storage first, then let versioned pipelines read and transform it.
Store only processed output and discard the raw input immediately.
Force every unknown future data structure into one rigid transactional schema before storage.
Overwrite raw inputs with transformed results so they cannot be replayed.
explain: Land immutable raw source data in Cloud Storage before transformation so future pipelines can replay and reinterpret it. Keeping only processed output loses information when schemas and analytical requirements change.

stem: You are creating a solution to remove backup files older than 90 days from your backup Cloud Storage bucket. You want to optimize ongoing Cloud Storage spend. What should you do?
options: Configure an age-based Delete lifecycle rule using supported JSON configuration or Terraform.
Keep a manual spreadsheet and delete a random selection each month.
Turn off all retention controls and assume old files disappear automatically.
Run a monthly manual deletion procedure even though deletion must follow each object reaching the age threshold.
explain: Set an age-based Delete lifecycle rule using supported JSON configuration or Terraform. Managed lifecycle policies avoid maintaining a recurring script that lists and removes objects manually.

stem: A legacy backend requires deduplicated, per-device ordered events. A Pub/Sub and Dataflow pipeline is planned. Which design avoids assuming unsupported global exactly-once delivery guarantees?
options: Use ordering keys where appropriate, event-time handling, explicit deduplication, and idempotent backend writes.
Assume selecting Pub/Sub plus Dataflow automatically guarantees global FIFO and exactly-once external side effects.
Sort messages only by arrival order and discard event timestamps.
Disable retries so any transient error permanently loses the event.
explain: Use Pub/Sub ordering keys where appropriate and Dataflow event-time processing with explicit deduplication and idempotent sinks. Neither product combination alone guarantees globally ordered exactly-once side effects across arbitrary external APIs.

stem: An API needs concurrent v1 and v2 releases under the same hostname and TLS certificate. Existing clients must keep working. How should requests be routed?
options: Use a URL map that routes versioned paths to separate backend services.
Silently forward every old API call to an incompatible new implementation.
Require a new certificate for every source commit.
Delete the v1 backend as soon as v2 is deployed.
explain: Route versioned URL paths to separate backend services through one Application Load Balancer. The existing hostname and certificate can remain while old and new APIs are deployed independently.

stem: Your operations team currently stores 10 TB of data m an object storage service from a third-party provider. They want to move this data to a Cloud Storage bucket as quickly as possible, following Google-recommended practices. They want to minimize the cost of this data migration. When approach should they use?
options: Download and re-upload objects with a manually operated CLI process without first considering a supported managed transfer.
Use the Storage Transfer Service to move the data
Download the data to a Transfer Appliance and ship it to Google
Download the data to the on-premises data center and upload it to the Cloud Storage bucket
explain: Storage Transfer Service supports managed transfers from supported object-storage sources to Cloud Storage. Routing data through an office connection or an appliance adds unnecessary hops for cloud-resident data.

stem: An API needs to accept bursts of 500,000 events per second and later serve low-latency exact-key lookups. The team wants managed request handling and a scalable serving database. Which combination fits, subject to quota and capacity planning?
options: Cloud Run and Bigtable.
Cloud Run and Cloud Storage as the sole millisecond-latency exact-key database for all records.
A single fixed VM and a flat file.
BigQuery as an unconditional single-digit-millisecond transactional key-value store.
explain: Cloud Run can scale request handling and Bigtable supports high-rate, low-latency key-based access. Design quotas, keys, buffering, and minimum capacity explicitly; Bigtable does not automatically scale to zero with an idle Cloud Run service.

stem: Your company runs several databases on a single MySQL instance. They need to take backups of a specific database at regular intervals. The backup activity needs to complete as quickly as possible and cannot be allowed to impact disk performance. How should you configure the storage?
options: Write a logical backup to separate high-throughput temporary storage, then verify and copy it to Cloud Storage; use a replica if source read impact must be isolated.
Write the only backup to the production data disk and assume there is no additional I/O.
Take an uncoordinated filesystem copy and assume it is always database-consistent.
Store the only backup on an unreplicated local SSD forever.
explain: Write a logical backup to separate high-throughput temporary storage, then upload it to durable Cloud Storage. This isolates backup-write I/O, but reading the source still consumes resources; use a replica if production impact must be minimized.

stem: All compute Engine instances in your VPC should be able to connect to an Active Directory server on specific ports. Any other traffic emerging from your instances is not allowed. You want to enforce this using VPC firewall rules. How should you configure the firewall rules?
options: Allow required Active Directory destinations and ports at priority 100, then explicitly deny other egress at priority 1000.
Deny all egress at priority 100, then allow Active Directory traffic at priority 1000.
Add only a low-priority allow and assume implied egress is deny-all.
Use ingress-only rules to block all outbound connections.
explain: Create a high-priority allow for required Active Directory destinations and ports plus a lower-priority explicit deny for other egress. Lower numeric priorities win, and the implied egress rule normally allows traffic.

stem: An existing GKE Standard node pool named workers must automatically scale between 1 and 10 nodes as scheduling demand changes. Which approach should the team use?
options: Enable the GKE cluster autoscaler for the workers node pool with --enable-autoscaling --node-pool=workers --min-nodes=1 --max-nodes=10 using the supported stable gcloud command.
Add a VM network tag named enable-autoscaling.
Resize the node pool once to ten nodes without enabling the cluster autoscaler.
Enable an independent Compute Engine autoscaler on the GKE-managed instance group.
explain: Enable autoscaling on the relevant node pool with minimum and maximum node counts using the supported gcloud command. Tags and one-time resize commands do not enable ongoing Kubernetes-aware node autoscaling.

stem: You need to deploy a stateful workload on Google Cloud. The workload can scale horizontally, but each instance needs to read and write to the same POSIX filesystem. At high load, the stateful workload needs to support up to 100 MB/s of writes. What should you do?
options: Use a persistent disk for each instance.
Use a regional persistent disk for each instance.
Create a Cloud Filestore instance and mount it in each instance.
Create a Cloud Storage bucket and mount it in each instance using gcsfuse.
explain: Filestore supplies managed NFS for applications needing concurrent POSIX file access across instances. Size the tier for throughput and availability; Cloud Storage FUSE is not a general replacement for POSIX filesystem semantics.

stem: You are creating an App Engine application that uses Firestore in Datastore mode as its persistence layer. You need to retrieve several root entities for which you have the identifiers. You want to minimize the overhead in operations performed by Firestore in Datastore mode. What should you do?
options: Create the Key object for each Entity and run a batch get operation
Create the Key object for each Entity and run multiple get operations, one operation for each entity
Use the identifiers to create a query filter and run a batch query operation
Use the identifiers to create a query filter and run multiple query operations, one operation for each entity
explain: Build entity keys and use a batch lookup when identifiers are already known. This avoids query-planning and index work and reduces round trips compared with separate reads.

stem: The development team has provided you with a Kubernetes Deployment file. You have no infrastructure yet and need to deploy the application. What should you do?
options: Create a GKE cluster, obtain credentials, and apply the Deployment YAML with kubectl.
Use kubectl to create the entire Google Cloud project and physical cluster with no cloud provisioning.
Upload Deployment YAML as an object and assume it becomes a running workload.
Run the container on one manually configured VM while ignoring the provided Deployment manifest.
explain: Provision a GKE cluster using gcloud or infrastructure as code, obtain credentials, then apply the Kubernetes manifest with kubectl. Infrastructure Manager manages Terraform resources; it does not interpret a Kubernetes Deployment YAML as a cloud deployment template.

stem: You are working with a data warehousing team that performs data analysis. The team needs to process data from external partners, but the data contains personally identifiable information (PlI). You need to process and store the data without storing any of the Pll data. What should you do?
options: Create a Dataflow pipeline to retrieve the data from the external source As part of the pipeline use the Sensitive Data Protection to remove any Pll data Store the result in BigQuery.

Create a Dataflow pipeline to retrieve the data from the external source As part of the pipeline store all non-PII data in BigQuery and store all Pll data in a Cloud Storage bucket that has a retention policy set.

Ask the external partners to upload an data on Cloud Storage Configure Bucket Lock for the bucket Create a Dataflow pipeline to read the data from the bucket As part of the pipeline, use the Cloud Data Loss Prevention (Cloud DIP) API to remove any Pll data Store the result in BigQuery.

Ask the external partners to import ail data in your BigQuery dataset Create a dataflow pipeline to copy the data into a new table As part of the Dataflow bucket skip all data in columns that have Pll data.
explain: Use a processing pipeline that inspects and de-identifies sensitive fields before persisting output to BigQuery. Saving raw PII to a staging bucket first violates a requirement to avoid storing it anywhere in the platform.

stem: Your company sends all Google Cloud logs to Cloud Logging. Your security team wants to monitor the logs. You want to ensure that the security team can react quickly if an anomaly such as an unwanted firewall change or server breach is detected. You want to follow Google-recommended practices. What should you do?
options: Schedule a cron job with Cloud Schedule The scheduled job queries the logs every minute for the relevant events.
Export logs to BigQuery, and trigger a query in BigQuery to process the log data for the relevant events.
Export logs to a Pub/Sub topic, and trigger Cloud Function with the relevant log events.
Export logs to a Cloud Storage bucket, and trigger Cloud Run with the relevant log events.
explain: Route relevant audit logs to Pub/Sub and invoke an authenticated response function. Event-driven routing reacts sooner than periodic batch queries; authorize, deduplicate, and audit any automated remediation.

stem: A healthcare team runs interruption-tolerant batch jobs on Google Cloud and must protect PHI under its BAA. Which approach combines cost management and appropriate service selection?
options: Use Spot capacity for suitable jobs and only BAA-covered services with required controls for PHI.
Assume provider certification makes every application configuration compliant.
Store PHI in any unrelated public service to reduce cost.
Disable retries and checkpointing for all batch jobs.
explain: Use Spot capacity for interruption-tolerant jobs and restrict protected health data to services covered by the BAA with the required controls. Provider service eligibility alone does not establish workload compliance.

stem: A Java application on a supported runtime fails at startup with ClassNotFoundException for a required third-party class. The application artifact does not include that dependency. What should the developer do?
options: Package the missing runtime dependency correctly, verify version compatibility, and redeploy.
Digitally sign every JAR and leave the dependency absent.
Change every SHA-256 hash to MD5.
Increase VM disk size without changing the artifact.
explain: A ClassNotFoundException identifies a missing runtime class or dependency. Package the required JAR and redeploy on a supported runtime; digitally signing every JAR does not supply the missing class.

stem: Your company has an application running as a Deployment in a Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) cluster When releasing new versions of the application via a rolling deployment, the team has been causing outages The root cause of the outages is misconfigurations with parameters that are only used in production You want to put preventive measures for this in the platform to prevent outages What should you do?
options: Configure liveness and readiness probes in the Pod specification
Configure an uptime alert in Cloud Monitoring
Create a Scheduled Task to check whether the application is available
Configure health checks on the managed instance group
explain: Readiness probes prevent traffic reaching pods that are not ready, and liveness probes can restart unhealthy containers. Node-group health checks cannot verify that a particular application has valid production configuration.

stem: Two organizations operate VPCs with non-overlapping subnet ranges. An application in one VPC needs direct private TCP connectivity to a service in the other, and both sides can configure networking. Which approach is suitable?
options: Configure VPC Network Peering on both sides with the required firewall rules and routes.
Use Shared VPC to attach any project from a different organization without migration.
Assume peering through a third VPC is automatically transitive.
Connect the VPCs through a common peer and assume peering forwards traffic transitively.
explain: VPC Network Peering can connect non-overlapping VPCs across organizations when both sides configure it and firewall rules permit traffic. Shared VPC is organization-scoped; peering is non-transitive.

stem: You have an outage in your Compute Engine managed instance group: all instance keep restarting after 5 seconds. You have a health check configured, but autoscaling is disabled. Your colleague, who is a Linux expert, offered to look into the issue. You need to make sure that he can access the VMs. What should you do?
options: Temporarily disable the faulty autohealing policy and grant the colleague narrow OS Login access, then diagnose and restore a corrected policy.
Keep recreating the VM every five seconds and expect a stable SSH session.
Restart the entire group repeatedly without preserving an instance for diagnosis.
Share one project-owner account with the colleague permanently.
explain: Temporarily disable the failing autohealing policy so the VM remains available for authorized diagnosis, then restore a corrected policy. Grant narrow access with OS Login rather than distributing a project-wide SSH key.

stem: You are designing an application for use only during business hours. For the minimum viable product release, you’d like to use a managed product that automatically “scales to zero” so you don’t incur costs when there is no activity. Which primary compute resource should you choose?
options: Cloud Run functions with minimum instances set to zero, accepting cold-start tradeoffs.
A Compute Engine VM left running around the clock.
A permanently provisioned single-node Kubernetes cluster.
App Engine flexible instances assumed to scale to zero.
explain: Cloud Run functions can scale to zero when there are no requests and minimum instances are zero. Account for cold starts and other service charges; VM instances and an always-on cluster retain provisioned costs.
