stem: Your company acquired a healthcare startup and must retain its customers’ medical information for up to 4 more years, depending on when it was created. Your corporate policy is to securely retain this data, and then delete it as soon as regulations allow. Which approach should you take?
options: Store the data in Google Drive and manually delete records as they expire.
Anonymize the data using the Sensitive Data Protection and store it indefinitely.
Store the data using the Cloud Storage and use lifecycle management to delete files when they expire.
Store the data in Cloud Storage and run a nightly batch script that deletes all expired datA.
explain: Use retention controls to prevent premature deletion and lifecycle rules to remove data after the allowed period. Select the correct object time basis and include recoverable versions and soft-delete policy in the retention design.

stem: A website portfolio collects bursty clickstream events and wants a low-cost durable raw archive for future batch analytics. It does not require serving individual clicks with millisecond database reads. Which storage service fits the archive?
options: Cloud Storage.
A VM local SSD as the only durable record.
A single in-memory cache as the sole archive.
A transactional database chosen only to hold compressed raw files.
explain: Cloud Storage offers durable, inexpensive retention of raw clickstream batches for future analysis. Use Pub/Sub and buffering for ingestion and BigQuery when interactive SQL analysis is needed; object storage is not a per-click query database.

stem: You are building a microservice- based application for TerramEarth. The application is based on Docker containers. You want to follow Google-recommended practices to build the application continuously and store the build artifacts. What should you do?
options: Trigger Cloud Build from source changes, build per-service images, and push immutable commit-associated artifacts to Artifact Registry.
Poll the repository manually and overwrite latest with no history.
Push executable containers only to an ordinary public object bucket and assume it provides registry metadata.
Compile every service separately on production VMs without recording source versions.
explain: Trigger Cloud Build from source changes, build each service, and store immutable, commit-associated images in Artifact Registry. Polling every minute and mutable latest tags weaken traceability and waste work.

stem: A web service stores each user's viewed-article list only in a server-side process variable. After traffic increases and the service scales out, users see articles they have already viewed. What is the most likely cause?
options: Session state is local to one instance and is not shared across instances.
Every new instance automatically overwrites all Firestore records.
The browser cannot connect to more than one IP address.
An HTTP Expires header synchronizes server-side memory.
explain: A session held in one instance's memory is lost or inconsistent when a request reaches another instance. Externalize state or use an appropriate stateless design rather than relying on instance affinity for correctness.

stem: An application development team believes their current logging tool will not meet their needs for their new cloud-based product. They want a bettor tool to capture errors and help them analyze their historical log data. You want to help them find a solution that meets their needs, what should you do?
options: Direct them to download and install the Cloud Operations logging agent.
Send them a list of online resources about logging best practices.
Help them define their requirements and assess viable logging tools.
Help them upgrade their current tool to take advantage of any new features.
explain: Gather the team's logging requirements before comparing tools: query patterns, retention, ingestion volume, security, and integration. Installing an agent alone does not establish that the solution meets those needs.

stem: You need to deploy an application on Google Cloud that must run on a Debian Linux environment. The application requires extensive configuration in order to operate correctly. You want to ensure that you can install Debian distribution updates with minimal manual intervention whenever they become available. What should you do?
options: Use VM Manager OS patch management with a tested patch schedule for the Debian VM.
Restart an old container without rebuilding its base image and assume packages update.
Manually recreate every VM for every security patch without automation.
Create a new instance template name without rebuilding the image or patching running VMs.
explain: Use VM Manager OS patch management with tested schedules for supported Debian VMs. A container restart does not update its base image; rebuild and redeploy immutable images when using containers instead.

stem: A GKE application already uses Cloud Service Mesh. Users report that calls across its microservices are slow. Which existing capability should the team inspect to locate the slow service edges?
options: Service mesh topology and request-latency telemetry.
Only Config Sync configuration commit counts.
Only the number of IAM folders.
Only object-storage lifecycle transitions.
explain: Use Cloud Service Mesh request telemetry and topology views to locate slow service edges. Config Sync manages configuration consistency; it does not diagnose request latency by inspecting YAML alone.

stem: Your team is developing a web application that will be deployed on Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE). Your CTO expects a successful launch and you need to ensure your application can handle the expected load of tens of thousands of users. You want to test the current deployment to ensure the latency of your application stays below a certain threshold. What should you do?
options: Run a representative concurrent-user load test and inspect latency, errors, saturation, and scaling behavior.
Enable autoscaling without testing and declare the latency objective met.
Send one curl request and treat it as a test of tens of thousands of users.
Inspect the architecture document and infer latency without exercising the application.
explain: Run a representative concurrent-user load test and measure latency and error rates. Enabling autoscaling is a configuration step, not evidence that the application meets its target under load.

stem: You company has a Kubernetes application that pulls messages from Pub/Sub and stores them in Firestore. Because the application is simple, it was deployed as a single pod. The infrastructure team has analyzed Pub/Sub metrics and discovered that the application cannot process the messages in real time. Most of them wait for minutes before being processed. You need to scale the elaboration process that is I/O-intensive. What should you do?
options: Use an HPA driven by appropriate Pub/Sub backlog metrics and processing demand, with capacity limits and node autoscaling as needed.
Scale a pull subscriber using only an unrelated push-request metric.
Enable only node autoscaling and assume it creates application replicas.
Increase only the Pub/Sub retention period without increasing consumer throughput.
explain: Scale consumers using subscription backlog and processing rate, with appropriate limits and resource requests. A push-request metric is unsuitable for a pull subscriber and node autoscaling alone does not add consumer replicas.

stem: Auditors visit your teams every 12 months and ask to review all the Google Cloud Identity and Access Management (Cloud IAM) policy changes in the previous 12 months. You want to streamline and expedite the analysis and audit process. What should you do?
options: Route Admin Activity audit logs to BigQuery with sufficient retention and provide auditors scoped read-only views.
Send the auditor only current IAM screenshots.
Delete older audit evidence before each annual visit.
Grant the auditor Owner so they can recreate missing history.
explain: Route Admin Activity audit logs to a queryable BigQuery dataset with sufficient retention and grant auditors scoped views. A Cloud Storage archive can retain evidence, but BigQuery simplifies repeated policy-change analysis.

stem: Your organization has decided to restrict the use of external IP addresses on instances to only approved instances. You want to enforce this requirement across all of your Virtual Private Clouds (VPCs). What should you do?
options: Set the compute.vmExternalIpAccess organization policy with the approved instance values.
Remove one subnet default route and assume it prohibits assigning external IPs.
Use Cloud NAT alone as an instance-creation restriction.
Create a project label named approved and assume it is enforced automatically.
explain: Enforce compute.vmExternalIpAccess centrally with approved instance values. Default routes and NAT govern traffic paths; they do not prohibit attaching an external IP during VM creation.

stem: You are working at an institution that processes medical data. You are migrating several workloads onto Google Cloud. Company policies require all workloads to run on physically separated hardware, and workloads from different clients must also be separated You created a sole-tenant node group and added a node for each client. You need to deploy the workloads on these dedicated hosts. What should you do?
options: Use node affinity labels targeting the specific sole-tenant node assigned to each client.
Use only the node-group name even if the group contains nodes shared among clients.
Use a network tag and assume it controls physical placement.
Disable scheduling constraints and rely on random placement.
explain: Use node affinity labels for the specific sole-tenant node when each client must occupy separate hardware. A label matching the entire node group can place different clients on the same node.

stem: You are monitoring Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) clusters in a Cloud Monitoring workspace. As a Site Reliability Engineer (SRE), you need to triage incidents quickly. What should you do?
options: Navigate the predefined dashboards in the Cloud Monitoring workspace, and then add metrics and create alert policies.
Navigate the predefined dashboards in the Cloud Monitoring workspace, create custom metrics, and install alerting software on a Compute Engine instance.
Write a shell script that gathers metrics from GKE nodes, publish these metrics to a Pub/Sub topic, export the data to BigQuery, and make a Data Studio dashboard.
Create a custom dashboard in the Cloud Monitoring workspace for each incident, and then add metrics and create alert policies.
explain: Start with the built-in GKE Monitoring dashboards and create actionable alert policies for service symptoms. A custom dashboard per incident adds delay and duplicate configuration.

stem: You are using Cloud SQL as the database backend for a large CRM deployment. You want to scale as usage increases and ensure that you don’t run out of storage, maintain 75% CPU usage cores, and keep replication lag below 60 seconds. What are the correct steps to meet your requirements?
options: Enable automatic storage increases; alert on CPU and replica lag; investigate and resize or tune based on the observed bottleneck.
Assume Cloud SQL CPU automatically scales to any requested target without configuration.
Preselect the largest machine forever and ignore replica lag.
Wait until storage is completely full before alerting.
explain: Enable automatic storage increases and alert on CPU utilization and replica lag. Resize or tune based on measured bottlenecks; storage growth is automatic only when configured, and sharding is not a universal replication-lag remedy.

stem: VPC A needs private communication with both VPC B and VPC C. All ranges are non-overlapping. A-to-B and B-to-C peering already exist, but A cannot reach C. What change addresses this?
options: Configure direct A-to-C peering and the required firewall and route settings.
Assume B forwards traffic transitively between its peers.
Add an IAM Viewer role and assume it creates a network path.
Add Cloud Router to VPC B and assume it turns VPC peering into a transit network.
explain: Use direct peering from the client VPC to each required peer VPC with non-overlapping ranges and matching firewall rules. Peering A-to-B and B-to-C does not create connectivity from A-to-C.

stem: A production database virtual machine on Compute Engine has an ext4-formatted persistent disk for data files The database is about to run out of storage space How can you remediate the problem with the least amount of downtime?
options: In the Cloud Platform Console, increase the size of the persistent disk and use the resize2fs command in Linux.
Shut down the virtual machine, use the Cloud Platform Console to increase the persistent disk size, then restart the virtual machine.
In the Cloud Platform Console, increase the size of the persistent disk and verify the new space is ready to use with the fdisk command in Linux.
In the Cloud Platform Console, create a new persistent disk attached to the virtual machine, format and mount it, and configure the database service to move the files to the new disk.
In the Cloud Platform Console, create a snapshot of the persistent disk, restore the snapshot to a new larger disk, unmount the old disk, mount the new disk, and restart the database service.
explain: Increase the persistent disk size and then grow the partition if necessary and the mounted ext4 filesystem with resize2fs. Increasing cloud disk capacity does not always expand the guest filesystem automatically.

stem: Your company has developed a monolithic, 3-tier application to allow external users to upload and share files. The solution cannot be easily enhanced and lacks reliability. The development team would like to re-architect the application to adopt microservices and a fully managed service approach, but they need to convince their leadership that the effort is worthwhile. Which advantage(s) should they highlight to leadership?
options: Explain independent delivery and scaling, managed operations, and maintainability while evaluating migration complexity and total cost.
Guarantee that microservices always cost less without measurement.
State that containers automatically create a complete CI/CD pipeline.
Claim that all application dependencies disappear after moving to a cloud VM.
explain: Explain independent delivery, scaling, maintainability, and managed-service operations, and assess migration cost and complexity. Microservices do not automatically reduce total cost or generate a CI/CD pipeline.

stem: Vehicle telemetry is stored in regional Cloud Storage buckets in the Americas, Europe, and Asia. One report needs data from every region. How can the team reduce cross-region data transfer for this report?
options: Preprocess and compress in each source region, then send the reduced dataset to the chosen analytical region.
Move every raw object to one region before doing any filtering.
Download every object through a developer laptop.
Duplicate all raw data into every region before every query.
explain: Preprocess and compress data in its source region, then transfer the reduced dataset to a chosen analytical region. This reduces inter-region data movement compared with relocating all raw telemetry first.

stem: Operational parameters such as oil pressure are adjustable on each of TerramEarth's vehicles to increase their efficiency, depending on their environmental conditions. Your primary goal is to increase the operating efficiency of all 20 million cellular and unconnected vehicles in the field How can you accomplish this goal?
options: Have your engineers inspect the data for patterns, and then create an algorithm with rules that make operational adjustments automatically.
Capture all operating data, train machine learning models that identify ideal operations, and run locally to make operational adjustments automatically.
Implement a Dataflow streaming job with a sliding window, and use Google Cloud Messaging (GCM) to make operational adjustments automatically.
Capture all operating data, train machine learning models that identify ideal operations, and host in Vertex AI to make operational adjustments automatically.
explain: Train centrally on fleet data and deploy an appropriate model to the vehicle for local inference. Local control can continue on disconnected vehicles and avoids depending on a round trip to the cloud for each adjustment.

stem: A retailer is piloting its application in Asia and wants to measure regional adoption, reliability, and user experience. Which metrics should it track?
options: Error rates for requests from Asia
Latency difference between US and Asia
Total visits, error rates, and latency from Asia
Total visits and average latency for users in Asia
The number of character sets present in the database
explain: Track adoption, latency, and errors for users in the target geography against explicit business and technical targets. Raw infrastructure utilization alone does not demonstrate improved user experience.

stem: Dress4Win has asked you to recommend machine types they should deploy their application servers to. How should you proceed?
options: Measure current demand, benchmark suitable machine types in a pilot, and right-size using observed performance and cost.
Always deploy the smallest instance to production first and wait for outages.
Select only by maximum RAM-to-CPU ratio regardless of workload.
Copy physical hardware core counts without measuring use.
explain: Start from measured workload requirements and benchmark candidate machine types in a safe pilot before production cutover. Then tune with Monitoring and Recommender; blindly choosing the smallest production VM risks outages.

stem: Your company is running its application workloads on Compute Engine. The applications have been deployed in production, acceptance, and development environments. The production environment is business-critical and is used 24/7, while the acceptance and development environments are only critical during office hours. Your CFO has asked you to optimize these environments to achieve cost savings during idle times. What should you do?
options: Use a managed instance schedule or authenticated scheduled automation to stop and start development and acceptance VMs while preserving required state.
Run an unmonitored administrative cron on a production application VM.
Delete all nonproduction disks after every workday.
Scale down only the database while keeping all nonproduction application VMs running at peak size.
explain: Schedule nonproduction instances to stop outside business hours and start before use, preserving required state. Avoid running administrative cron jobs on production application VMs when a managed schedule suffices.

stem: Your company is planning to upload several important files to Cloud Storage. After the upload is completed, they want to verify that the upload content is identical to what they have on- premises. You want to minimize the cost and effort of performing this check. What should you do?
options: Compare local CRC32C checksums with the uploaded Cloud Storage object checksums using supported tools.
Download the entire dataset again as the only way to validate integrity.
Compare only filenames and ignore file contents.
Assume the upload is correct whenever a bucket exists.
explain: Compare local CRC32C checksums with Cloud Storage object checksums using supported tooling. This verifies integrity without downloading the entire dataset and paying unnecessary transfer costs.

stem: You are tasked with building an online analytical processing (OLAP) marketing analytics and reporting tool. This requires a relational database that can operate on hundreds of terabytes of data. What is the Google recommended tool for such applications?
options: Cloud Spanner, because it is globally distributed
Cloud SQL, because it is a fully managed relational database
Cloud Firestore, because it offers real-time synchronization across devices
BigQuery, because it is designed for large-scale processing of tabular data
explain: BigQuery is the warehouse for large OLAP queries. Spanner's transactional consistency and global scale address a different problem and are not a reason to use it for hundred-terabyte marketing scans.

stem: Your operations team currently stores 10 TB of data m an object storage service from a third-party provider. They want to move this data to a Cloud Storage bucket as quickly as possible, following Google-recommended practices. They want to minimize the cost of this data migration. When approach should they use?
options: Use the gcloud storage mv command lo move the data
Use the Storage Transfer Service to move the data
Download the data to a Transfer Appliance and ship it to Google
Download the data to the on-premises data center and upload it to the Cloud Storage bucket
explain: Use Storage Transfer Service for supported cloud object-store sources. Direct managed transfer avoids staging data on-premises or arranging physical shipping for data already in a cloud provider.

stem: Compute Engine instances in a private subnet have no external IPs. They must initiate HTTPS requests to public third-party APIs. Which service supplies outbound connectivity without exposing inbound public addresses?
options: Cloud NAT configured for the private subnet.
Private Google Access alone for every arbitrary internet host.
IAP TCP forwarding as a general outbound NAT service.
Private services access to a managed database instead of outbound internet NAT.
explain: Use Cloud NAT for private instances that must initiate connections to public internet destinations. Private Google Access covers supported Google APIs, and IAP is for authorized inbound administration.

stem: Your web application must comply with the requirements of the European Union’s General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR). You are responsible for the technical architecture of your web application. What should you do?
options: Ensure that your web application only uses native features and services of Google Cloud,because Google already has various certifications and provides “pass-on” compliance when you use native features.
Enable the relevant GDPR compliance setting within the Google CloudConsole for each of the services in use within your application.
Ensure that Cloud Security Scanner is part of your test planning strategy in order to pick up any compliance gaps.
Define a design for the security of data in your web application that meets GDPRrequirements.
explain: Translate the organization's privacy requirements into access, deletion, retention, encryption, and data-handling controls. There is no universal console setting or provider certification that makes an application GDPR-compliant automatically.

stem: You are building a microservice- based application for TerramEarth. The application is based on Docker containers. You want to follow Google-recommended practices to build the application continuously and store the build artifacts. What should you do?
options: Trigger Cloud Build from source changes, build per-service images, and push immutable commit-associated artifacts to Artifact Registry.
Poll the repository manually and overwrite latest with no history.
Push executable containers only to an ordinary public object bucket and assume it provides registry metadata.
Build directly on production VMs and overwrite previous image tags with no immutable digest history.
explain: Create builds from source events and tag or associate each microservice image with its commit; deploy by immutable digest from Artifact Registry. A mutable latest tag or polling timestamp alone does not establish source-to-production provenance.

stem: Your company has multiple on-premises systems that serve as sources for reporting. The data has not been maintained well and has become degraded over time. You want to use Google-recommended practices to detect anomalies in your company data. What should you do?
options: Profile cloud-staged data with BigQuery SQL and managed data-quality scans, then apply tested, versioned cleaning rules.
Ignore missing values and assume migrating to the cloud fixes them.
Delete random rows until the dataset gets smaller.
Validate only whether files are encrypted and skip schema, missingness, and duplicate checks.
explain: Profile representative data for missing values, duplicates, outliers, and schema inconsistencies, then apply versioned cleaning rules. BigQuery SQL and managed data-quality scans can inspect cloud-staged data without a retired notebook or preparation service.

stem: Your company has an application running on a deployment in a GKE cluster. You have a separate cluster for development, staging and production. You have discovered that the team is able to deploy a Docker image to the production cluster without first testing the deployment in development and then staging. You want to allow the team to have autonomy but want to prevent this from happening. You want a Google Cloud solution that can be implemented quickly with minimal effort. What should you do?
options: Create a Kubernetes admission controller to prevent the container from starting if it is not approved for usage in the given environment.
Configure a Kubernetes lifecycle hook to prevent the container from starting if it is not approved for usage in the given environment.
Implement a corporate policy to prevent teams from deploying Docker image to an environment unless the Docker image was tested in an earlier environment.
Configure the binary authorization policies for the development, staging and production cluster Create attestations as part of the continuous integration pipeline”.
explain: Use Binary Authorization with attestations from successful test stages to enforce promotion requirements. A written policy or container startup hook alone cannot provide equivalent admission control.

stem: Your company is designing its application landscape on Compute Engine. Whenever a zonal outage occurs, the application should be restored in another zone as quickly as possible with the latest application data. You need to design the solution to meet this requirement. What should you do?
options: Use an instance template and regional persistent disk; fence the old writer and recover in the surviving replication zone.
Restore the latest snapshot into the same unavailable zone.
Assume regional disks synchronously replicate across all regions worldwide.
Keep all current data only on the failed VM's local SSD.
explain: Use a regional persistent disk and reproducible instance template to recover in the other replication zone, fencing the prior writer. Restoring a snapshot in the failed zone neither restores availability nor guarantees the latest writes.

stem: An existing GKE Standard node pool named workers must automatically scale between 1 and 10 nodes as scheduling demand changes. Which approach should the team use?
options: Enable the GKE cluster autoscaler for the workers node pool with --enable-autoscaling --node-pool=workers --min-nodes=1 --max-nodes=10 using the supported stable gcloud command.
Add a VM network tag named enable-autoscaling.
Resize the cluster to ten nodes once and assume it will shrink automatically.
Enable an independent Compute Engine autoscaler on the GKE-managed instance group.
explain: Enable the GKE node pool's cluster autoscaler using supported stable gcloud flags and set appropriate bounds. One-time resizing and resource tags do not implement automatic capacity changes.

stem: You are developing an application using different microservices that should remain internal to the cluster. You want to be able to configure each microservice with a specific number of replicas. You also want to be able to address a specific microservice from any other microservice in a uniform way, regardless of the number of replicas the microservice scales to. You need to implement this solution on Google Kubernetes Engine. What should you do?
options: Use a Deployment for each microservice and a ClusterIP Service with stable internal DNS.
Expose every individual pod directly through a public external IP.
Use external Ingress as the only internal service-discovery mechanism.
Pin clients permanently to pod IPs and never update them.
explain: Use a Deployment per microservice and a ClusterIP Service for stable DNS and load balancing. Pod names and IPs change; an external Ingress is unnecessary for traffic that must remain internal.

stem: Recipients of a chat message must be able to verify that a particular user signed its content and that it has not been altered. Which mechanism provides that property?
options: Digitally sign messages and their relevant context with the sender's private key and verify using its authenticated public key.
Encrypt every message with one shared key and assume this proves the individual sender.
Add a user name to unsigned plaintext and trust it.
Use TLS alone and assume it gives recipient-verifiable signatures for stored messages.
explain: Digitally sign the message and relevant context with the sender's private key, then verify with the authenticated public key. Encryption with a shared key does not prove which participant sent a message; signing is distinct from encryption.

stem: A game needs a managed store for high-volume activity time series with low-latency key-range reads. Which service is the best fit?
options: Bigtable
Cloud Spanner
BigQuery
Firestore in Datastore mode
explain: Bigtable is designed for scalable time-series and key-range access. Choose row keys for the required queries and write distribution; a warehouse is better for large analytical scans than low-latency serving reads.

stem: A racing team wants feature attributions to understand why its Vertex AI model makes particular predictions and use those findings to guide validated improvements. Which capability should it use?
options: Vertex Explainable AI.
Cloud Vision OCR as a generic explanation of every model.
Cloud Monitoring CPU charts as feature attributions.
An object lifecycle rule that retrains every model automatically.
explain: Use Vertex Explainable AI feature attributions to investigate predictions and identify potential data or modeling problems. Explanation supports analysis but does not automatically increase prediction accuracy.

stem: A portal publishes latency-sensitive events to Pub/Sub. Measurements show that client-side batching wait accounts for most publish timeouts, while quotas and subscriber capacity are healthy. What change should the team evaluate first?
options: Increase the Pub/Sub Total Timeout retry value.
Move from a Pub/Sub subscriber pull model to a push model.
Turn off Pub/Sub message batching.
Create a backup Pub/Sub message queue.
explain: For latency-sensitive publishing, reduce or disable batching after measuring batch wait and RPC behavior. This trades throughput and cost efficiency for lower delay; distinguish a batching timeout from subscriber processing or quota issues.

stem: A game backend is moving to an elastic Google Cloud architecture with much higher expected player concurrency. How should its testing strategy change?
options: Tests should scale well beyond the prior approaches.
Unit tests are no longer required, only end-to-end tests.
Tests should be applied after the release is in the production environment.
Tests should include directly testing the Google Cloud infrastructure.
explain: Test beyond the prior platform's capacity using realistic concurrency, data, and dependency behavior. Cloud hosting does not remove the need for unit tests, preproduction testing, or failure drills.

stem: A migration copies data from 24 on-premises source VMs over a complex internet path and one VPN tunnel to 4 destination VMs, then Cloud Storage. Which THREE parts should be measured first as potential throughput constraints?
options: The capacity of the single VPN tunnel.
Internet path latency, loss, and effective bandwidth.
Destination-worker CPU, disk, and network capacity.
The cold storage class selected for archive retention after transfer, when archive reads are not on the transfer path.
The retention duration of completed archive objects, when no objects are being overwritten or deleted.
The period of the completed data-retention audit, without checking migration network or worker metrics.
explain: End-to-end throughput is limited by network capacity, path quality, and destination processing capacity. Measure each segment before adding resources; a storage class change alone does not remove a VPN or destination-worker bottleneck.

stem: At Dress4Win, an operations engineer wants to create a tow-cost solution to remotely archive copies of database backup files. The database files are compressed tar files stored in their current data center. How should he proceed?
options: Schedule checksum-verified copies to a suitable cold Cloud Storage class with the required retention policy.
Keep the only backup on the database VM's local SSD.
Move files before verifying uploads and immediately destroy all recovery copies.
Keep a permanently running large database solely to hold compressed archive files.
explain: Schedule verified copies to Cloud Storage with an appropriate cold storage class and retention policy. Keep a recoverable source copy until upload integrity is verified; select the class using access frequency and retrieval cost.

stem: Your company is developing a web-based application. You need to make sure that production deployments are linked to source code commits and are fully auditable. What should you do?
options: Record the source commit and build provenance for an immutable image digest, and record that digest in production deployment history.
Use only a mutable latest tag for every deployment.
Ask developers to remember which commit they last deployed.
Change commit timestamps after production deployment.
explain: Associate an immutable artifact digest with the source commit and build provenance, and record the deployed digest. A tag containing a commit is useful but must not be the only control because tags can be moved.

stem: Your application needs to process credit card transactions. You want the smallest scope of Payment Card Industry (PCI) compliance without compromising the ability to analyze transactional data and trends relating to which payment methods are used. How should you design your architecture?
options: Create a tokenizer service and store only tokenized data.
Create separate projects that only process credit card data.
Create separate subnetworks and isolate the components that process credit card data.
Streamline the audit discovery phase by labeling all of the virtual machines (VMs) that process PCI data.
Enable Logging export to BigQuery and use ACLs and views to scope the data shared with the auditor.
explain: Tokenize payment details and keep raw card data inside the protected vault and processing boundary. Downstream analytics can use non-sensitive tokens, but tokenization design and compliance scope still require assessment.

stem: A lead software engineer tells you that his new application design uses websockets and HTTP sessions that are not distributed across the web servers. You want to help him ensure his application will run property on Google Cloud. What should you do?
options: Help the engineer to convert his websocket code to use HTTP streaming.
Review the encryption requirements for websocket connections with the security team.
Meet with the cloud operations team and the engineer to discuss load balancer options.
Help the engineer redesign the application to use a distributed user session service that does not rely on websockets and HTTP sessions.
explain: Review WebSocket support, connection timeouts, backend draining, and session behavior with operations. Use distributed session state where correctness requires it; load-balancer affinity alone cannot preserve state through instance failure.

stem: You are deploying an application on App Engine that needs to integrate with an on- premises database. For security purposes, your on-premises database must not be accessible through the public Internet. What should you do?
options: Use Cloud VPN or Interconnect plus the selected App Engine runtime's supported VPC connectivity to reach the private database.
Use App Engine ingress firewall rules as if they create an outbound private route.
Publish the database on the internet and rely on its hostname remaining secret.
Embed database administrator credentials in public JavaScript.
explain: Use private hybrid connectivity plus the runtime's VPC integration: Serverless VPC Access for App Engine standard, or native VPC networking for flexible. App Engine ingress firewall settings do not create a route to an on-premises database.

stem: A campaign website collects signup details. Demand ranges from a few requests to large spikes, and the team wants managed compute and a serverless document database. Which combination is appropriate?
options: Cloud Run for the website/API and Firestore for the form data.
One fixed-capacity VM with no scaling plan.
A self-managed cluster whose nodes are manually provisioned per signup.
A manually administered web and database VM kept at fixed capacity for all traffic spikes.
explain: Cloud Run with Firestore provides managed, elastic serving and storage for a simple campaign. Configure quotas and abuse controls; a fixed VM or self-managed cluster adds operational burden for highly variable traffic.

stem: Your company wants to track whether someone is present in a meeting room reserved for a scheduled meeting. There are 1000 meeting rooms across 5 offices on 3 continents. Each room is equipped with a motion sensor that reports its status every second. The data from the motion detector includes only a sensor ID and several different discrete items of information. Analysts will use this data, together with information about account owners and office locations. Which database type should you use?
options: Flat file
NoSQL
Relational
Blobstore
explain: A scalable NoSQL store can hold frequent room-status updates keyed by room and time. Select Firestore for current state or Bigtable for high-volume time series based on actual access patterns rather than treating all NoSQL engines as identical.

stem: Your company pushes batches of sensitive transaction data from its application server VMs to Pub/Sub for processing and storage. What is the Google- recommended way for your application to authenticate to the required Google Cloud services?
options: Ensure that VM service accounts are granted the appropriate Pub/Sub IAM roles.
Ensure that VM service accounts do not have access to Pub/Sub, and use VM access scopes togrant the appropriate Pub/Sub IAM roles.
Generate an OAuth2 access token for accessing Pub/Sub, encrypt it, and store it in Cloud Storage for access from each VM.
Create a gateway to Pub/Sub using a Cloud Function, and grant the Cloud Function service account the appropriate Pub/Sub IAM roles.
explain: Grant the VM's attached service account the required Pub/Sub role and use Application Default Credentials. Access scopes do not replace IAM, and cached manually generated tokens add avoidable credential handling.

stem: Your company places a high value on being responsive and meeting customer needs quickly. Their primary business objectives are release speed and agility. You want to reduce the chance of security errors being accidentally introduced. Which two actions can you take?
options: Ensure every code check-in is peer reviewed by a security SME.
Use source code security analyzers as part of the CI/CD pipeline.
Ensure you have stubs to unit test all interfaces between components.
Enable code signing and a trusted binary repository integrated with your CI/CD pipeline.
Run a vulnerability security scanner as part of your continuous-integration /continuous- delivery (CI/CD) pipeline.
explain: Automate source-code analysis and vulnerability scanning as pipeline checks, with triage and enforcement appropriate to risk. Automation provides fast repeatable feedback without requiring every routine commit to wait for a specialist review.

stem: Your company is designing its application landscape on Compute Engine. Whenever a zonal outage occurs, the application should be restored in another zone as quickly as possible with the latest application data. You need to design the solution to meet this requirement. What should you do?
options: Use an instance template and regional persistent disk; fence the old writer and recover in the surviving replication zone.
Restore the latest snapshot into the same unavailable zone.
Use only a cross-region asynchronous copy and assume it provides synchronous two-zone recovery with no data loss.
Keep all current data only on the failed VM's local SSD.
explain: A regional persistent disk keeps synchronous replicas in two zones within one region. Recover the VM in a surviving replication zone using an instance template; it is not a cross-region disk-replication solution.

stem: You are designing a large distributed application with 30 microservices. Each of your distributed microservices needs to connect to a database back-end. You want to store the credentials securely. Where should you store the credentials?
options: In the source code
In an environment variable
In a secret management system
In a config file that has restricted access through ACLs
explain: Store database credentials in Secret Manager with per-workload IAM, rotation, and audit logging. Source code and ordinary configuration files spread secrets; prefer identity-based database authentication when supported.

stem: Your company's user-feedback portal comprises a standard LAMP stack replicated across two zones. It is deployed in the us-central1 region and uses autoscaled managed instance groups on all layers, except the database. Currently, only a small group of select customers have access to the portal. The portal meets a 99.99% availability SLA under these conditions However next quarter, your company will be making the portal available to all users, including unauthenticated users. You need to develop a resiliency testing strategy to ensure the system maintains the SLA once they introduce additional user load. What should you do?
options: Replay representative sanitized traffic until all relevant tiers scale, then simulate a zonal failure in a controlled test and measure recovery.
Introduce random production failures without authorization or a recovery plan.
Test only one homepage request and assume every tier scales.
Measure only total VM count without application latency or errors.
explain: Replay representative sanitized traffic until all scalable tiers are exercised, then simulate a zonal failure in an authorized test. Measure recovery, database behavior, and user latency, rather than relying only on a utilization threshold.

stem: Your customer is moving their corporate applications to Google Cloud. The security team wants detailed visibility of all projects in the organization. You provision the Google Cloud Resource Manager and set up yourself as the org admin. What Google Cloud Identity and Access Management (Cloud IAM) roles should you give to the security team'?
options: Grant organization visibility and only the necessary project read-only roles, preferably through a group.
Grant Owner on every project for a read-only review.
Grant organization administration simply to view resource configuration.
Share the billing administrator's password with every analyst.
explain: Grant organization visibility and the minimum project-level read permissions required by the security team. Viewer roles reveal configuration without giving them the ability to modify resources; avoid Owner or organization-admin grants for simple inspection.

stem: You have an application deployed on Kubernetes Engine using a Deployment named echo- deployment. The deployment is exposed using a Service called echo- service. You need to perform an update to the application with minimal downtime to the application. What should you do?
options: Use kubectl set image deployment/echo-deployment CONTAINER=IMAGE_DIGEST and monitor the rolling rollout.
Delete the Deployment and then recreate it for each release.
Update the VM node-group image instead of the application image.
Delete the Service so clients must wait for a new endpoint.
explain: Update the Deployment image and let its rolling-update strategy and readiness probes control replacement. Modifying the node-group image updates infrastructure, not the application Deployment.

stem: A team wants to reduce VM management. It has simple HTTP containers and a second workload that requires Kubernetes APIs. Which TWO managed compute products should it evaluate for these respective needs?
options: Cloud Run for the HTTP containers.
GKE Autopilot for the Kubernetes workload.
A hand-built Kubernetes control plane on unmanaged VMs.
A single desktop process for both workloads.
A permanently running oversized VM with no orchestration.
explain: Choose Cloud Run for serverless container hosting and GKE Autopilot when Kubernetes APIs and workload controls are required. Both reduce infrastructure work, but Autopilot still requires Kubernetes workload operations and is not literally no-ops.

stem: You are analyzing and defining business processes to support your startup’s trial usage of Google Cloud, and you don’t yet know what consumer demand for your product will be. Your manager requires you to minimize Google Cloud service costs and adhere to Google best practices. What should you do?
options: Train the team on cost management, use eligible free-tier allowances, set budgets and alerts, and avoid commitments until a baseline is understood.
Buy peak-demand commitments before measuring demand.
Use budget notifications as the only guardrail and assume they automatically cap all service usage.
Disable all cost visibility until the trial ends.
explain: Train teams on cost management, use eligible free-tier allowances, and monitor consumption before committing to uncertain baseline demand. Set budgets and alerts, but remember budgets do not generally cap resource usage automatically.

stem: Your company has just acquired another company, and you have been asked to integrate their existing Google Cloud environment into your company’s data center. Upon investigation, you discover that some of the RFC 1918 IP ranges being used in the new company’s Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) overlap with your data center IP space. What should you do to enable connectivity and make sure that there are no routing conflicts when connectivity is established?
options: Create a Cloud VPN connection from the new VPC to the data center, create a Cloud Router, and apply new IP addresses so there is no overlapping IP space.
Create a Cloud VPN connection from the new VPC to the data center, and create a Cloud NAT instance to perform NAT on the overlapping IP space.
Create a Cloud VPN connection from the new VPC to the data center, create a Cloud Router, and apply a custom route advertisement to block the overlapping IP space.
Create a Cloud VPN connection from the new VPC to the data center, and apply a firewall rule that blocks the overlapping IP space.
explain: Renumber overlapping RFC 1918 ranges before joining the networks with ordinary routed VPN connectivity. Cloud Router exchanges routes; firewall rules cannot make identical destination ranges unambiguous.

stem: A game backend contains many independently deployable containerized microservices. It needs immutable artifacts, quick rollback, and redundant GKE serving with HTTP routing. Which platform combination fits?
options: Artifact Registry, GKE, and an external Application Load Balancer through GKE Gateway or Ingress.
Cloud Storage, a scheduled shell script, and manually started VM containers without a deployment controller.
One manually modified VM with mutable files and no artifact history.
Cloud Build and Cloud Storage without a container runtime or workload orchestration platform.
explain: Store container artifacts in Artifact Registry and deploy independent GKE workloads with suitable Gateway or Ingress routing. Versioned images and rollout controls support quick rollback; an object bucket alone does not provide container artifact management.

stem: Your company wants you to build a highly reliable web application with a few public APIs as the backend. You don’t expect a lot of user traffic, but traffic could spike occasionally. You want to leverage Cloud Load Balancing, and the solution must be cost-effective for users. What should you do?
options: Cloud Storage for static origin assets, Cloud Run for APIs, a suitable managed database, and an external Application Load Balancer with optional Cloud CDN.
Cloud CDN alone as durable storage for all user data.
A large permanently running GKE Standard cluster solely for a rarely used simple API.
A single unbacked local SSD serving all static content and database records.
explain: Use Cloud Storage for static assets and Cloud Run for the API, with a suitable managed database and external Application Load Balancer. Cloud CDN is a cache rather than durable origin storage; a large always-on cluster is unnecessary for sporadic traffic.

stem: You are building a continuous deployment pipeline for a project stored in a Git source repository and want to ensure that code changes can be verified deploying to production. What should you do?
options: Build one immutable artifact, deploy it to staging, run required tests, and promote the same digest through the production pipeline.
Deploy untested code to 10% of production as the only verification step.
Rebuild a different artifact for production without testing it.
Rebuild from an unpinned source branch during production deployment without validating the new artifact.
explain: Build a single immutable artifact, deploy it to staging, run tests, and promote the same digest to production with approvals where required. A production canary adds protection but does not replace verification before production.

stem: Cloud CDN serves identical static content over HTTP and HTTPS, and the origin response does not vary by protocol. What cache-key change can improve reuse when it is supported and safe for this content?
options: Omit protocol from the cache key after validating response equivalence.
Shorten all cache lifetimes to zero.
Add a random per-request identifier to every cache key.
Use an imaginary Cache-Region header as a routing policy.
explain: Exclude an unnecessary cache-key component only when it cannot change the response; serving identical HTTP and HTTPS content may permit omitting the protocol. Shorter TTLs generally reduce cache reuse, and there is no Cache-Region routing header.

stem: You are creating an App Engine application that uses Firestore in Datastore mode as its persistence layer. You need to retrieve several root entities for which you have the identifiers. You want to minimize the overhead in operations performed by Firestore in Datastore mode. What should you do?
options: Create the Key object for each Entity and run a batch get operation
Create the Key object for each Entity and run multiple get operations, one operation for each entity
Use the identifiers to create a query filter and run a batch query operation
Run a separate identifier-filtered query for each entity instead of a key-based lookup.
explain: Use a batch get by known entity keys. Filtering queries by identifiers performs unnecessary query work, while individual gets add round trips compared with one lookup batch.

stem: Your web application uses Google Kubernetes Engine to manage several workloads. One workload requires a consistent set of hostnames even after pod scaling and relaunches. Which feature of Kubernetes should you use to accomplish this?
options: StatefulSets
Role-based access control
Container environment variables
Persistent Volumes
explain: A StatefulSet provides stable pod ordinal identities and hostnames, commonly with a headless Service. A PersistentVolume preserves data but does not by itself provide stable pod network identities.

stem: An existing 10 TB database export must be copied to Cloud Storage. A usable 1 Gbps connection is available and there is no requirement that forces offline transfer. How should the team minimize additional database load and avoid shipping delays?
options: Compress the existing files and upload them in parallel with resumable transfer and checksum validation.
Re-query the production database once for each destination object.
Order an appliance without evaluating online throughput or lead time.
Run all files through a single slow serial application proxy.
explain: Compress the existing export and upload in parallel over the usable 1 Gbps link after measuring throughput. An appliance adds lead time and handling costs that are not justified solely by a 10 TB dataset.

stem: You have an application that makes HTTP requests to Cloud Storage. Occasionally the requests fail with HTTP status codes of 5xx and 429. How should you handle these types of errors?
options: Use gRPC instead of HTTP for better performance.
Implement retry logic using a truncated exponential backoff strategy.
Make sure the Cloud Storage bucket is multi-regional for geo-redundancy.
Monitor https://status.cloud.google.com/feed.atom and only make requests if Cloud Storage is not reportingan incident.
explain: Use capped exponential backoff with jitter for retryable 429 and 5xx responses and ensure retries are safe. Changing to gRPC or choosing a different bucket location does not remove throttling or transient failure semantics.

stem: Your applications will be writing their logs to BigQuery for analysis. Each application should have its own table. Any logs older than 45 days should be removed. You want to optimize storage and follow Google recommended practices. What should you do?
options: Configure the expiration time for your tables at 45 days
Make the tables time-partitioned, and configure the partition expiration at 45 days
Rely on BigQuery’s default behavior to prune application logs older than 45 days
Create a script that uses the BigQuery command line tool (bq) to remove records older than 45 days
explain: Use time-partitioned tables with a 45-day partition expiration policy. Whole-table expiration deletes the entire table; partition expiration removes old time slices while retaining recent logs.
